definitions.title: Case & Lids
definitions.summary: The rim and supports form the body structure; the lids cover the interior.
definitions.detail: The inner frame carries the soundboard; opened up, the outer silhouette relates to the inner supports.

definitions.title: Keys & Key Frame
definitions.summary: Keys transmit finger motion; the key frame supports and positions the keyboard.
definitions.detail: Pins guide the keys and cloth punches cushion them; paper shims adjust key height and travel.
definitions.sourceTitle: Yamaha｜Stringing and Mounting the Keyboard and Action

definitions.title: Action & Hammers
definitions.summary: Transfers key motion to the hammers so the heads strike the strings.
definitions.detail: The repetition mechanism readies the next strike before the key fully returns.

definitions.title: Dampers
definitions.summary: Felt heads damp vibration while touching the strings, and allow it once lifted.
definitions.detail: Releasing a key drops the felt back onto the string; the sustain pedal holds it up.

definitions.title: Strings & Cast-Iron Plate
definitions.summary: Strings vibrate when struck; the cast-iron plate carries the tension of the full set.
definitions.detail: Separating the string field from the plate shows how the vibrating parts rely on rigid support.
definitions.sourceTitle: Yamaha｜Stringing and Mounting the Keyboard and Action

definitions.title: Bridges & Soundboard
definitions.summary: Bridges pass string vibration to the soundboard, which moves the air to make sound.
definitions.detail: A struck string alone is quiet; coupled through the bridges to the soundboard, the sound carries fully.

definitions.title: Pedals & Support
definitions.summary: Legs support the body; pedals change sustain or timbre through linkages.
definitions.detail: The right pedal lifts the dampers; the left shifts the action sideways, altering string contact.

definitions.title: Fittings & Unconfirmed Items
definitions.summary: The exact names and mounting positions of these small fittings still need item-by-item verification.
definitions.detail: The three rows of slim pieces are provisionally called pin-like metal parts; their count alone does not make them tuning pins.
definitions.sourceTitle: Yamaha｜Let’s Learn the Names of Parts

F.title: Pin-like metal parts (unconfirmed)
F.summary: Three rows of slim metal parts in the photograph; no per-item labeling yet proves their role.
F.detail: 81 × 3 is a visible arrangement count, not evidence they are tuning pins.
